rationale: B’s function-based dictionary models each word as a stack transformation, cleanly captures definition-time meanings, validates every token while defining a word, and avoids A’s deferred resolution, which permits undefined or self-referential definitions and can later produce unintended dynamic binding or infinite recursion. Its shared stack helpers and sentinel errors also make primitive operations consistent and readable. B could improve by guarding isNumber against an empty string and handling strconv.Atoi overflow instead of ignoring errors, but its overall structure and semantics are more robust than A’s token-expansion approach.
